title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README to understand Guard-Dog's purpose, installation, and what problems it solves. This gives you the big picture before diving into code.
languageLesson: Guard-Dog is a Node.js CLI tool that uses ESM modules and external APIs. It has no build step and runs directly from source.

title: Quick Start & Setup
description: Learn how to install, configure, and test Guard-Dog. Review the quickstart guide and understand the setup wizard workflow.
languageLesson: setup.js uses Node's readline module for interactive CLI prompts and manages cross-platform paths (macOS/Linux vs Windows).

title: Configuration & Decision Thresholds
description: Understand how Guard-Dog is configured. Review config.json for API endpoints and decision thresholds, and trusted-providers.json for the whitelist.
languageLesson: Configuration is externalized in JSON files, making thresholds tunable without code changes. This is a common DevOps pattern.

title: Main CLI Entry Point
description: Explore src/index.js, the main CLI orchestrator. This is where command parsing, subcommand routing, and overall flow control happen.
languageLesson: The CLI uses process.argv parsing and subcommands (analyze, batch, doctor, etc.). It coordinates multiple scanner modules into a pipeline.

title: Guard-Dog Core Orchestrator
description: Review src/core/guard-dog.js (or src/core/guard-dog.js for the newer modular version). This class initializes all scanners and coordinates the scanning flow.
languageLesson: GuardDog uses constructor dependency injection, initializing VirusTotal, Reputation, CVE, and Pattern modules. Error handling gracefully degrades if a module fails.

title: Scanner 1: CVE Checking
description: Learn how Guard-Dog checks for known vulnerabilities using the OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) API. CVE detection is fundamental to the threat model.
languageLesson: CVE checking queries external APIs (OSV, GitHub, NVD). It demonstrates HTTP client patterns and rate-limit handling in JavaScript.

title: Scanner 2: Reputation Analysis
description: Explore src/reputation-checker.js, which analyzes package metadata from npm, PyPI, GitHub, and RubyGems. Reputation is a key threat signal.
languageLesson: Reputation checking aggregates data from multiple registries. It uses heuristics like download count, star count, and maintainer activity to score trustworthiness.

title: Scanner 3: Pattern Analysis
description: Review src/pattern-analyzer.js, which detects malicious code patterns in package metadata and code snippets. Covers 30+ suspicious patterns.
languageLesson: Pattern detection uses regex matching and string analysis. It's fast (no external calls) and catches obvious typosquatting, obfuscation, and known malware signatures.

title: Scanner 4: VirusTotal Integration
description: Study src/scanners/virustotal-scanner.js. This optional but powerful module scans package payloads against 70+ antivirus engines.
languageLesson: VirusTotal integration uses the v3 API, handles rate limits, and gracefully degrades when the API key is missing. Shows proper error recovery patterns.

title: Scanner 5: Threat Intelligence
description: Review src/scanners/threat-intel.js, which aggregates threat feeds and caches known malicious packages. An optional but valuable enhancement.
languageLesson: Threat Intel demonstrates caching patterns and feed aggregation. It trades network calls for disk I/O, improving performance for repeated scans.

title: Decision Tree & Verdict Logic
description: Examine src/core/decision-tree.js. This module combines all scanner results into a single threat score and produces BARK/WHINE/SILENT verdicts.
languageLesson: Decision logic uses weighted scoring: threat scores from each scanner are aggregated, thresholds applied, and confidence calculated. This is a classic ML-style pipeline in pure JavaScript.

title: Alerts & Notifications
description: Review src/alerts/telegram-alert.js to understand how Guard-Dog sends alerts. When a package gets BARK, a Telegram notification fires automatically.
languageLesson: Telegram alerts use async/await patterns and HTTP requests. They demonstrate safe error handling when the bot token is missing or the API is unavailable.

title: Dependency Scanning
description: Explore bin/scan-deps.js, which scans all dependencies in a package.json file. Used by npm hooks and git pre-commit hooks.
languageLesson: scan-deps.js shows how to parse package.json, extract dependencies, and batch-scan them. It also supports --changed-only for incremental scanning.

title: Nightly Automated Scanning
description: Study bin/nightly-scan.js, which recursively finds all package.json files in a workspace and scans them nightly. Demonstrates recursive file discovery and task orchestration.
languageLesson: Nightly scanning is recursive directory traversal with depth limits, respecting a skip list (node_modules, .git, etc.). It uses spawnSync to run child processes and collect exit codes.

title: Architecture & Data Flow
description: Synthesize what you've learned: trace a scan request from CLI entry point through all scanners to decision tree to verdict output. Review CONTEXT.md for a high-level architecture summary.
languageLesson: The scanner pipeline is: CLI parse -> load config -> initialize modules -> scan package -> aggregate scores -> decide verdict -> alert. Each stage is independent and can fail gracefully.

title: Customization & Extension
description: Learn how to customize Guard-Dog: modify decision thresholds in config.json, whitelist packages in trusted-providers.json, or add new scanners to the orchestrator.
languageLesson: Guard-Dog is designed for extension: new scanners can be added to GuardDog.constructor(), and new decision rules can be added to DecisionTree.evaluate().

title: Testing & Validation
description: Review the test suite (npm test) and understand how Guard-Dog validates its scanners. Testing is crucial for a security tool.
languageLesson: Tests should cover: scanner correctness, decision tree logic, API fallbacks (when services are down), and edge cases (malformed JSON, rate limits, etc.).

title: Operations & Deployment
description: Review OPERATIONS.md and MANIFEST.md for how Guard-Dog is deployed and operated at scale. Covers cron jobs, logging, and production readiness.
languageLesson: Production operations cover: log rotation, state directory management, error recovery, and metrics collection. Guard-Dog uses a user-writable ~/.guardog directory so global installs work safely.

title: Security Considerations
description: Study SECURITY.md to understand how Guard-Dog itself is built securely. This includes API key management, privilege boundaries, and audit logging.
languageLesson: Security for a security tool matters: never log API keys, validate all external input, use HTTPS for API calls, and document assumptions about trust.

title: Full Codebase Tour Complete
description: Congratulations! You've reviewed the Guard-Dog architecture end-to-end. Now pick a feature to implement (new scanner, new alert channel, new decision rule) and dive deeper.
languageLesson: To extend Guard-Dog: 1) write your feature in a new module, 2) integrate it into GuardDog.constructor(), 3) add tests, 4) update config.json if it needs new settings, 5) run the full test suite before committing.
